_about.purpose: Labelled corpus for measuring scorer accuracy, calibration and fairness. Replayed by `python -m app.evaluate`.
_about.labelling: expected_winner is a human judgement by the project author, not adjudicated ground truth. Cases a careful reader cannot decide on the evidence alone are labelled null and excluded from accuracy; they are reported separately as the abstention set. Cases G026 onward were added to widen the corpus; they are weighted toward contested and adversarial shapes on purpose, because adding easy cases would lift the accuracy figure without making it more informative.
_about.difficulty: clear = one side is obviously right | contested = both sides have real evidence | adversarial = constructed to break a specific heuristic | unarbitrable = not decidable on the evidence
_about.fields: evidence entries are [submitted_by, evidence_type, raw_content] filed_on pins the dispute date for cases where return-window arithmetic matters; without it those cases age against the real clock and silently change answer.

cases.rationale: Perishable goods claim the merchant never rebutted; support acknowledged contact but produced no counter-evidence.

cases.claim_text: This item wasn't what I ordered.

cases.claim_text: I was charged twice for the same order.

evidence: Delivered to 900 Industrial Pkwy, Warehouse District, signed by Receiving Dept.

evidence: Package scanned at regional facility 2026-05-20, in transit to destination.
cases.rationale: In transit for over a month with no further scan; non-delivery is the reasonable inference.

cases.claim_text: Merchant admitted the item was defective in chat but never refunded me.
evidence: We apologize for the defective unit and will process this for you.
Refunds are provided within 14 days for defective items.
cases.rationale: Merchant admitted the defect and its own policy mandates a refund that was never issued.

cases.claim_text: Package was returned to sender apparently, but I was home all day.
evidence: Package returned to sender after failed delivery attempt.
cases.rationale: Goods went back to the merchant, so the card member paid for nothing.

cases.claim_text: Item arrived damaged and merchant provided a photo showing packaging was fine.
evidence: Photo shows the shipping box fully intact with no visible damage.
cases.rationale: Only positive evidence is the merchant's intact-packaging photo; the card member produced nothing.

cases.claim_text: Charged twice, and merchant already refunded one charge via email confirmation.
evidence: We've confirmed and refunded the duplicate charge as requested. Sorry for the trouble!
cases.rationale: The duplicate was already refunded. Awarding the card member here is a double refund; the apology must not read as an unremedied admission.

cases.claim_text: Item shows delivered and signed, but the box was empty when I opened it.

evidence: Delivered to 99 Pine Ave, Rivertown, signed by unknown recipient.
cases.rationale: Same street and city, different building, plus a generic signee. Token-overlap address matching scores this for the merchant.

cases.claim_text: This was delivered to a completely different state.
evidence: Delivered to 5 Elm St, Denver, signed by R. Patel.
cases.rationale: Different street and different city. Shares only the house number and 'st', which token overlap treats as a match.

cases.claim_text: Carrier left it somewhere without any signature and I never found it.

evidence: You were charged twice in error. The second charge has been refunded in full on 2026-06-14.
